From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & quick wins: Acme model-comparison sprint

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a concise set of follow-ups so we can move into a short comparative sprint next week: 

What we heard on the call:
- Primary goal: pick an inference stack that minimizes hallucination for product Q&A and keeps per-token cost predictable at scale.
- Constraints: 2-week PoC window, data residency in US, procurement contact Lucas (cc).

Proposed next tests (short, measurable):
1) Quality: 50 domain prompts (you mentioned you can share) run against Redwood, Bedrock, and Vertex; compute exact-match, F1, and hallucination flags.
2) Regression probes: 10 adversarial prompts we saw on the call (edge cases + long-context).
3) Performance: 95th percentile latency at batch sizes 1/4/16 and token throughput.
4) Cost-sensitivity: token-cost breakdown with and without KV/prefix caching enabled.

Connor will help own the test harness and give a short tech plan. Attached are my notes from today
(attachment: acme-demo-notes.pdf).

Ask: could you send the sample prompt set and a minimal success criteria doc by EOD Friday so we can lock the sprint plan?

Thanks — looking forward.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear summary. Attaching the initial 50 prompts we can share internally (attachment: acme-50-sample-prompts.txt). We've also noted the success criteria (high-level): <60% hallucination rate on product facts, avg latency <300ms for interactive traffic, and cost target TBD after the first run.

Procurement: Lucas will surface any legal/procurement constraints after the technical results. For now, please assume standard MSA review and US-only data retention.

I'll coordinate with Lucas to confirm the final ownership for the sprint. Can we schedule the run for next Tuesday (23rd)?

Thanks,
Sara

Acme Corporation

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & quick wins: Acme model-comparison sprint

Sara / Hannah —

Thanks for the prompt set, Sara — I pulled it in and skimmed. Below is a proposal for a minimal, repeatable harness we can run within the two-week PoC window.

Technical plan (high-level):
- Harness: small python runner that hits each endpoint with identical prompt+system prefixes. Produces per-prompt QA metrics and token-level logs.
- Endpoints to compare: Redwood (redwood-hosted model variant), AWS Bedrock (model X/v1), GCP Vertex AI (model Y/v2).
- Measures: exact-match, normalized F1, hallucination flag (annotated heuristics + human sampling), latency p50/p95/p99, token consumption.
- Caching configuration: run Redwood with KV cache ON and OFF to show unit-economics delta.
- Quantization/precision: test Redwood int8 vs float16 to measure quality delta for long-context prompts.

Data handling / compliance:
- We will run in US-only regions; logs can be redacted before sharing. If you need an NDA addendum for the sample prompts, flag it and Hannah will coordinate.

Schedule suggestion:
- Fri 19 Jun: finalize prompt set + success criteria.
- Mon 22 Jun: test harness dry run on internal synthetic set.
- Tue 23 Jun: full run with ACME prompts; deliver initial report Wed 24 Jun.

Attached is a small reference prompt bank we use for MAPS-style regression checks (attachment: MAPS_test_prompts.txt).

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
